decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans, as set out in the attached schedule which forms part of this notice. Location PlanPlanning Design & Access StatementPlanning Precedent & Policy Support StatementDaylight, Sunlight & Overshadowing AssessmentTransport Statement2025-18-PA-JC - 001 A2025-18-PA-JC - 002 A2025-18-PA-JC - 003 A2025-18-PA-JC - 004 A2025-18-PA-JC - 005 A2025-18-PA-JC - 006 A2025-18-PA-JC Ex-OS2025-18-PA-JC - OS2570 - 01 Rev CReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture those of the existing building, unless otherwise specified in the approved application. Reason: To ensure a design which complies with Development Plan Policies.

Prior to first occupation, a detailed Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Submitted details will demonstrate the maximum achievable energy efficiency achievable for the development and shall provide for the maximum achievable improvements in the total CO2 emissions arising from the operation of a development and its services over part L of Building Regs 2013. The Energy Statement should outline how the reductions are achieved through the use of Fabric Energy Efficiency performance, energy efficient fittings, and the use of renewable technologies. In line with Policy DMD49, the CO2 savings of the proposal shall not be less than 35%.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The development must achieve reduced water consumption through the use of water efficient fittings, appliances and recycling systems to result in consumption equal to or less than 105 litres per person per day.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Core Policy 21 of the Core Strategy and the London Plan.

Prior to first occupation, details of the design of refuse storage facilities, including facilities for the recycling of waste to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The refuse storage shall be provided within the development in accordance with the London Borough of Enfield Waste and Recycling Planning Storage Guidance ENV 08/162.In particular, waste collection vehicles must be able to get within 25 m of the refuse storage point. Residents should not have to carry waste further than 30 m.Reason: To ensure the efficient, safe and clean removal of household refuse, and to ensure that the location and accessibility of refuse storage maintains safety on the highway.

Notwithstanding the provisions of classes A, B, C, D, E and F of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (or any amending Order), no enlargement, improvement, alteration, buildings, extensions or enclosure to the existing and new buildings hereby approved shall be carried out or erected without the prior approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and ensure that the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and to prevent the overdevelopment of the site.

Prior to occupation, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority, cycle parking shall be provided in compliance with the following criteria:- A minimum of 2 long stay cycle parking spaces must be provided.- Cycle parking must be located in an accessible position. The access route to the store must be a minimum of 1.2 m wide, step free, and involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door), each of which must have a minimum clear opening width of 1.2 m.- Cycle parking must be secure, including a British Standard mortice lock or access fob.- Cycle parking must be fully enclosed, with 4 walls and a roof.Reason: To support the Council's Climate Action and Transport Policies which aim to increase the use of active and sustainable transport modes. Easy and secure access to bicycle parking is required to remove barriers to cycling.

The boundary wall enclosing the front garden area of No. 88A Connaught Avenue shall be permanently retained in accordance with the details shown on drawing No. 2570-01 Rev C.Reason: To ensure highway safety and to prevent illegal crossing and unsafe vehicle movements

Prior to the commencement of any construction work, a detailed Drainage Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall be based on the disposal of surface water by means of a sustainable drainage system in accordance with the Technical Guidance to the National Planning Policy Framework and the SuDS requirements set out in Policy DMD 61.The submitted details shall include:- Revised discharge calculations demonstrating a runoff rate that reflects the true greenfield runoff rate for the 1 in 1 year and 1 in 100 year (plus climate change) events.- Where a greenfield rate cannot be achieved, details of a two stage flow control and/or orifice based flow control system designed to reduce runoff to the lowest practicable rate.- Evidence that lower discharge rates have been considered and are achievable where extensive source control SuDS measures are used across the site, with the aim of treating 100 percent of hardstanding runoff.- A drainage plan drawing showing all SuDS features, pipe runs, flow directions and outfall locations.- Cross sections, dimensions, materials and specifications for each proposed SuDS feature, including rain gardens, attenuation storage, permeable paving, swales and planters.- Details of overland exceedance flow routes, including spot levels, demonstrating how surface water will safely bypass buildings and reach appropriate areas during exceedance events.- A SuDS management and maintenance plan, including inspection schedules, responsibilities and arrangements for long term management.The development shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the approved details and shall be retained and maintained thereafter.Reason: To ensure the development provides an appropriate and sustainable surface water drainage system, reduces flood risk, minimises surface water discharge outside the site and ensures that the system remains functional for the lifetime of the development, in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policy DMD 61 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), Policies SI12 and SI13 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework.
